mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate economic growth and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following low FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate suggests economic weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer and business confidence declines.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the 20-day periods following a UNRATE increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates improving consumer demand and economic expansion, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns in the short term.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 50% of the 5-day periods following a HOUST increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production suggests supply chain disruptions or reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day periods following an INDPRO decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and retail sales indicates strong consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as businesses expand production and hiring.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 20-day periods following simultaneous increases in HOUST and RSAFS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high federal funds rates and low unemployment suggests tight monetary conditions, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase and consumer spending slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day periods following the trigger conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth indicates a robust economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings and consumer spending increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day periods following strong GDP growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in non-farm payroll employment suggests a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 5-day periods following a PAYEMS increase, the hypothesis is rejected.
